title: Going To a Place: Hová? and the Suffix -ra/-re

sections.content: Hová means 'to where' -- it asks about a destination, not a location. The place you're heading to takes the sublative suffix -ra or -re (vowel harmony decides which), meaning roughly 'onto/to'.
Keep Hol (where at) and Hová (where to) apart: 'Hol van az állomás?' asks about location, but 'Hová megyünk?' asks about a destination and expects a -ra/-re answer, not a plain van answer.
